$description: Enforcement actions. Three orthogonal status axes: action_status (what the authority did and whether it stands), payment_status (whether money moved), remedy_status (whether behaviour changed). Nothing in this schema permits 'fine imposed' to imply 'fine collected'.
$note: null means the question has not been researched. 'unknown' means it has been researched and is not publicly determinable. These are different states and must never be rendered alike. No aggregate totals are stored here: any total shown to a user is computed from these records at render time. The pipeline stages shown in the interface are DERIVED from these fields by a documented rule set (js/pipeline.js), not stored, so no stage can be asserted that the record does not support. A stage the record cannot settle is Unknown, and Unknown is never counted as zero. AUDIT-2026-09-25 (2026-09-26): records re-read individually against their sources carry that date in their own last_verified; this file's $last_verified is deliberately unchanged, because the file as a whole was not re-read, and moving it would assert that it was.

judicial.outcome: The CNPD's decision was annulled in all its parts and the file remitted to the CNPD: it had not examined fault (intent or at least negligence), which the CJEU requires (C-807/21 Deutsche Wohnen and C-683/21 Nacionalinis: the GDPR sets no strict liability), and it had treated a fine as the only option, without weighing the other measures available under Art. 58. On the merits the Court confirmed, for the practices at the start of the investigation, that Art. 6(1)(f) was not a sufficient legal basis and that Arts 12–14 were breached, and confirmed Arts 15–17 subject to the reservation that rectification and erasure were at risk rather than shown to be infringed; it held that the investigation's scope did not cover Arts 16 and 21. The CNPD itself declared its injunctions moot, the last changes it asked for having been made. Judgment of 12 March 2026 (ECLI:LU:CADM:2026:52757), published 13 March 2026.

enforcement.verification_note: Verified 2026-09-27 against the judgment itself (Cour administrative, 52757C, 12 March 2026, 89 pages, read in full text from the Luxembourg administrative courts' site). It confirms the CNPD decision of 15 July 2021, the EUR 746,000,000 fine with a daily penalty of EUR 746,000, the grounds of annulment, the findings on the merits and the injunctions becoming moot, which supports remedy:implemented. The judgment is pseudonymised ('(AA)'); that the appellant is Amazon Europe Core rests on the Luxembourg judiciary's announcement of 13 March 2026 and the press reports that name it. The CNPD decision date was corrected from 16 to 15 July 2021 on 2026-09-26 and is confirmed by the judgment.

appeal.note: Appeal lodged on 25 April 2025 against the judgment of the tribunal administratif of 18 March 2025 (no. 46578 du rôle), which had dismissed the challenge to the CNPD decision. Decided 12 March 2026: the decision annulled in all its parts and the file remitted. The Cour administrative describes itself in the judgment as the second and last instance. What the CNPD does on remittal is not established.

judicial.outcome: Voided on a pure jurisdiction point: once OpenAI established an Irish subsidiary, the Irish DPC became lead authority under the one-stop-shop. Nine months of investigative work produced no ruling on whether the conduct was lawful.

enforcement.verification_note: Corrected 2026-09-27 from the Garante's own website. The decision is no. 755 of 2 November 2024 (doc-web 10085455); 20 December 2024, recorded here before, is the date of the Garante's press release announcing it (doc-web 10085432), which confirms the EUR 15 million fine, the six-month information campaign ordered under Art. 166(7) of the Italian Privacy Code, an investigation opened in March 2023, and the transfer of the file to the Irish DPC as lead authority once OpenAI established its European headquarters in Ireland. The same notice records that the Court of Rome's judgment no. 4153/2026, published 18 March 2026, upheld OpenAI's opposition. STILL OPEN: the judgment itself has not been read, so its ground — recorded as a jurisdiction point under the one-stop-shop — rests on academic analysis (European Law Blog). The judicial outcome's 'nine months of investigative work' does not match the Garante's account of an investigation opened in March 2023 and decided in November 2024; what the nine months measure is not established.

appeal.note: Decided: the Garante's own notice (read 27 Sep 2026) states that the Court of Rome's judgment no. 4153/2026, published 18 March 2026, upheld OpenAI's opposition to decision no. 755, and that the decision has been temporarily removed from the Garante's website. Whether the Garante has appealed is not established.

enforcement.action: Non-compliance decision and fine under Art. 5(4)
enforcement.behavioural_outcome: EU iPhone users can set rival browsers and payment apps as defaults, install applications outside the App Store, and use third-party payment solutions.
enforcement.verification_note: Updated 2026-09-27. The appeal is now established from the Official Journal notice of the action (Case T-438/25, lodged 7 July 2025) and the Court's register (pending on 27 Sep 2026); the investigation's opening date, 25 March 2024, is from the Commission's press release IP/25/1085, read in full the same day. STILL OPEN: the behavioural outcome recorded here reproduces the author's interpretation (clm-dma-consumer-benefit-modest) and is not what this decision is about — the press release describes a steering infringement under Art. 5(4) and an order to remove technical and commercial restrictions on steering within 60 days; it says nothing about default browsers, installation outside the App Store or third-party payment. The same release closed the separate investigation into Apple's user-choice obligations. Establishing what changed for users after this decision needs a Commission compliance assessment, which has not been read.

judicial.forum: General Court of the European Union
judicial.outcome: Apple's designation challenges dismissed in full. App Store and iOS obligations confirmed; iMessage pleas held inadmissible; App Store versions treated as a single core platform service. Closes the route by which designated gatekeepers could contest interoperability obligations at the designation stage, but leaves the substance of Art. 6(7) untested.
judicial.case_ref: Joined Cases T-1079/23, T-1080/23 and T-214/24, ECLI:EU:T:2026:451

enforcement.verification_note: Judicial outcome checked on 27 Sep 2026 against the judgment itself (ECLI:EU:T:2026:451): operative part point 2 dismisses the actions; paras 47 and 62 hold the plea of illegality against Art. 6(7) inadmissible at the designation stage; para 99 rejects the plea against treating the App Stores as a single core platform service; para 133 holds the iMessage plea inadmissible; para 148 dismisses the actions in T-1079/23 and T-214/24 as inadmissible. Whether an appeal to the Court of Justice has been lodged is still not established (see appeal.note). Until 27 Sep 2026 action_status read action:final, which the unknown appeal contradicts; it reads action:imposed and the pipeline shows its final stage as unknown rather than reached.
